title: Feature/2159
summary: People who never set a display name used to show up as a code like "User 2a3f34d6". Now they're named after their avatar's color and picture, for example "Red Forest (Anonymous)", everywhere names appear (session participants, the Profile page, the Friends list). A brand-new account is asked once, right after first sign-in, to choose a name or keep that default. Clicking a person in a session's participant list opens their profile, which now shows their **User ID** with a **Copy** button.

links.label: Issue 2159: Users without a display name are shown as "User <id>" with no way to view the user ID

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link at the top of this page in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page looks like an older version, do a hard refresh: Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, or Cmd+Shift+R on Mac.

setup.title: Have a few brand-new email addresses ready
setup.body: The name prompt only appears for accounts that have never signed in before, so you'll need **three email addresses that have never been used with Seed Bible**. Signing in sends a code to the address, so you must be able to read its inbox. With Gmail you can add `+` and any word before the `@` and the mail still reaches you: for example `yourname+sb1@gmail.com`, `yourname+sb2@gmail.com`, `yourname+sb3@gmail.com`.

setup.title: Have an existing account with a name
setup.body: You'll also need one account that already has a display name set (your usual Seed Bible account is fine).

setup.title: Use private windows for a clean start
setup.body: Do each new-account test in a fresh private (incognito) window, opened on the preview link. Close the private window when you're done with that account, so the next one starts clean.

sections.title: Choosing a name after first sign-in
sections.intro: A brand-new account is asked once to pick a name or keep the default based on its avatar.

tests.title: A brand-new account is asked to choose a display name
tests.why: Issue 2159 asks for new users to be prompted to choose a name or keep the default.
tests.before: Use your first brand-new email address, in a fresh private window. On a phone, a card about installing the app may appear first; close it and the name prompt should appear after.
steps: Sign in with your first brand-new email address and enter the code from your inbox.
Wait a few seconds after signing in.
expected: A window titled **Choose a display name** appears, saying "Others will see this name in sessions. You can keep the default from your avatar, or pick your own."

It shows a round avatar (a colored circle with a small picture, such as a tree, leaf, dog or coffee cup) next to a default name made of a color and a word plus "(Anonymous)", for example `Red Forest (Anonymous)`.
Below that is a box labeled **Your name**, showing the same default name in grey, with the typing cursor already in it.
There are two buttons: **Keep default** and **Save name**.
Write down the default name shown; later tests use it.

tests.title: Keep default closes the prompt and uses the avatar name
tests.before: Continue from the previous test, with the prompt still open.
steps: Choose **Keep default**.
Open your **Profile** (from the app's menu or sidebar).
expected: The prompt closes.
Your Profile shows the default name you wrote down (for example `Red Forest (Anonymous)`), not a code of letters and numbers.

tests.title: The prompt doesn't come back after choosing Keep default
tests.before: Still signed in as the first new account.
steps: Reload the page.
Wait a few seconds, then close the tab and open the preview link again in the same private window.
expected: The **Choose a display name** window does not appear again.
Your Profile still shows the same default name.

tests.title: Typing a name and choosing Save name uses that name
tests.before: Close the private window from the earlier tests. Open a new private window on the preview link and use your second brand-new email address.
steps: Sign in with your second brand-new email address.
When **Choose a display name** appears, type `Test Reader` in the **Your name** box.
Choose **Save name**.
Open your **Profile**.
Reload the page and wait a few seconds.
expected: The prompt closes after **Save name**.
Your Profile shows `Test Reader`.
After the reload, the prompt does not appear again and the name is still `Test Reader`.

tests.title: The prompt comes back if you reload without answering, and Escape keeps the default
tests.why: The prompt should keep asking until it's answered, and pressing Escape counts as keeping the default.
tests.before: Close the private window from the previous test. Open a new private window on the preview link and use your third brand-new email address. This test needs a keyboard.
steps: Sign in with your third brand-new email address.
When **Choose a display name** appears, don't choose anything. Reload the page.
When the prompt appears again, press the **Esc** key.
Reload the page once more.
expected: After the first reload, the prompt appears again.
Pressing **Esc** closes it.
After the last reload, the prompt doesn't appear, and your Profile shows the color-and-word default name.

tests.title: An existing account with a name isn't asked
tests.before: Close the private window. Open a new private window on the preview link.
steps: Sign in with your existing account that already has a display name.
Wait a few seconds.
expected: No **Choose a display name** window appears.
Your Profile shows your existing name, unchanged.

tests.title: The prompt fits on a phone screen and in dark mode
tests.before: You need one more brand-new email address for this test (for example `yourname+sb4@gmail.com`). Skip it if you don't have one.
steps: On a phone, open the preview link in a private tab, with the phone set to dark mode.
Sign in with the new email address and wait for **Choose a display name**.
Tap the **Your name** box so the keyboard opens.
expected: The whole window fits on the screen: the title, the avatar and default name, the box and both buttons can all be seen (scrolling a little is fine).
Text is easy to read on the dark background, and the long default name isn't cut off in a way that hides the color or the word.
Both **Keep default** and **Save name** can be tapped.

sections.title: Names and user IDs in a shared session
sections.intro: These tests use two browsers side by side: one signed in as the first new account (default name), one as your existing named account.

setup.title: Two browsers, two accounts
setup.body: Browser A: a private window signed in as your **first** new account (the one that kept the default name). Browser B: a different browser, or a normal (non-private) window, signed in as your existing named account. Put them side by side if you can.

tests.title: Your own entry shows your avatar name instead of "User" and a code
tests.why: Issue 2159 reports entries like "User 2a3f34d6 (you)"; it asks for a default name built from the avatar's color and icon.
steps: In browser A, open **John 3**.
Choose the **Share** button (the share icon at the top of the tabs) and then **Start and share session**.
Copy the invite link it gives you.
Look at the participants list (**Participants · 1**) under the tab. On a phone, tap the small stack of avatars near the top of the reader to open it.
expected: Your entry reads as your default name followed by "(you)", for example `Red Forest (Anonymous) (you)`.
It's the same default name you wrote down in the first test, and the avatar beside it has the same color and picture as in the prompt.
Nothing in the list shows "User" followed by a code.

tests.title: Clicking your own entry shows your user ID with a Copy button
tests.why: Issue 2159 asks that the user ID can be viewed, for example by clicking the entry.
steps: In browser A's participants list, click your own name.
In the **Profile** window that opens, find the **User ID** line.
Choose **Copy** next to it.
Paste into any text box (for example the browser's address bar) to see what was copied, then delete it.
expected: A **Profile** window opens with your avatar and default name.
Below them is a line labeled **User ID**, followed by a long code of letters and numbers.
After **Copy**, a short confirmation appears, and what you paste matches the code shown.

tests.title: Another person sees you by the same avatar name
steps: Close the Profile window in browser A.
In browser B, open the invite link you copied and join the session.
In browser B, look at the participants list (now **Participants · 2**).
In browser A, look at the participants list too.
expected: In browser B, the first account shows the same default name as in browser A (for example `Red Forest (Anonymous)`), with the same avatar color and picture.
In browser B, your named account shows its real name with "(you)".
In browser A, the named account shows its real name.
No entry shows "User" followed by a code, and no entry shows an avatar with no name beside it.

tests.title: Clicking another participant shows their user ID
steps: In browser B, click the first account's default name in the participants list.
Choose **Copy** next to **User ID**, and paste it somewhere to check it.
expected: A **Profile** window opens showing the first account's avatar, default name and a **User ID** line.
The User ID matches the one you saw in browser A in the earlier test.

tests.title: Names and avatars stay the same after reloading
tests.why: Avatars in a session are now based on the account rather than the browser tab, so they should stay the same when someone reloads or rejoins.
steps: Note the avatar color and picture each browser shows for the first account.
In browser A, reload the page and wait for the session to reconnect.
Look at the participants list in both browsers again.
expected: In both browsers, the first account has the same default name, avatar color and picture as before the reload.
The participant count doesn't go up to 3 (there may be a brief moment while it reconnects).

tests.title: A signed-out guest gets an avatar name too
steps: Open a third window that is signed out (a new private window in another browser, or close browser A's private window and open a new one).
Without signing in, open the session invite link and join.
In browser B, look at the participants list.
expected: The guest shows as a color-and-word name with "(Anonymous)", for example `Blue Leaf (Anonymous)`, next to a matching avatar.
Nothing shows "User" followed by a code.

tests.title: A person without a name shows their avatar name in Friends
tests.before: Browsers A (first new account) and B (named account) are in the same session again. If you closed browser A, sign in as the first new account again and rejoin.
steps: In browser B's participants list, choose **Add friend** next to the first account's name to send a friend request.
In browser A, open **Friends** and find the incoming request.
In browser B, open **Friends** and find the sent request.
expected: In browser B, the request to the first account shows its default color-and-word name (the same one as in the session), not "User" followed by a code.
In browser A, the request from the named account shows its real name.

tests.title: Changing your name later updates it everywhere
steps: In browser A, open **Profile** and choose **Edit profile**.
In **Profile name**, type `Second Name`, then choose **Save changes**.
Look at your entry in the session participants list in browser A, and at the first account in browser B.
expected: Your Profile shows `Second Name`.
Within a few seconds, both browsers show `Second Name` instead of the default name.
The **Choose a display name** window does not appear.

notCovered: Names shown on answers to discussion questions inside a session, and in session chat, for a person without a name. These now use the same color-and-word name, but reaching them takes a session with question steps.
Accounts created before this change that never set a name aren't shown the prompt (it's only for the first sign-in of a new account); they simply get the color-and-word name.
Other languages: the color and picture words are translated only where translators have already done so.
Code reorganisation with no visible effect (the avatar color list moved to its own file) and the unit test updates.
